title: Multiple LLM Agents Debate for Equitable Cultural Alignment
benchmark_measurement: Adherence to social etiquette norms in cultural groups defined partly by religious identity (e.g., African Islamic, Catholic Europe, Orthodox Europe, Protestant Europe). The benchmark, NORMAD-ETI, was validated in part by religious leaders.
findings: Multi-agent debate frameworks improve cultural alignment and parity across different cultural groups. The paper found that models struggle to align with scenarios from 'African Islamic' and 'Orthodox Europe' cultural groups, and the proposed debate method helps benefit these underrepresented groups, achieving closer parity scores.
